expert.preview: The quantum saving comes from comparing candidates before paying to verify one. The classical obstruction is that a query to the planted cell must name an address formed from independent hard answers. Trace the weighted pivot law and the separate-cap prediction bound, then see where their exponents meet.
expert.question: What lets this construction pass the cubic separation from earlier cheat sheets?

exposition.audience: General mathematical readers familiar with probability and linear algebra
exposition.preview: Imagine a board with one winning column. A classical algorithm can spend almost all its queries finding the right square to inspect. A quantum algorithm can compare two columns cheaply before checking a short list of candidates. Follow a four-column example through both searches to see why the gap approaches a fourth power.
exposition.question: How much can a quantum algorithm save when both algorithms have to read the same hidden bits?
